problem: The v1 pipeline truncates each survey independently to extreme-tail/top candidates before cross-survey reasoning, so moderate but spatially consistent morphology can be lost even when multiple surveys measure the same feature.

order: compute frozen morphology metrics at every eligible center independently in each survey
convert each metric and existing generic robust score to within-survey empirical percentiles
align eligible centers on common Earth-fixed grid without using target labels
aggregate spatially aligned percentile evidence across surveys before any per-survey top-K truncation
only then spatially deduplicate and cap follow-up candidates
v2_mechanism.rationale: Two independent survey-local upper-5-percent events have nominal product-tail 0.0025, comparable to or stricter than the previous single-survey 0.005 extreme-tail gate, while allowing moderate repeatable evidence to survive.
v2_mechanism.family_evidence: family percentile = maximum empirical percentile among frozen metrics belonging to that morphology family
cross_survey_candidate_rule: at least two distinct surveys have generic percentile >= 0.95 at aligned support
OR at least two distinct surveys have the same structural family percentile >= 0.95

ranking.primary: product of the two smallest survey-local generic tails; lower is stronger
ranking.tertiary: number of morphology families supported in at least two surveys

spatial_alignment.grid_or_match_tolerance: must be fixed from survey sampling density before metric values are inspected

nuisance_controls: preserve beam-edge and coverage validity filters
do not count multiple products derived from the same acquisition as independent surveys
retain survey-local percentile values and raw family evidence for audit

metrics: known-target recall where independent truth exists
